result.question: Model Mimir Labs' next 6 months: MRR generation, burn (incl. COGS), runway, and whether/when the $500K pre-seed closes — month by month.

report.question: Model Mimir Labs' next 6 months: MRR generation, burn (incl. COGS), runway, and whether/when the $500K pre-seed closes — month by month.

prediction.headline: A partial ~$300–400K pre-seed triggers at month 6 on the strength of two engaged manufacturers, first paid services, and a closing-momentum narrative — but with a 1-month close lag, cash actually lands in month 7, just outside the 6-month horizon. In-horizon, the round is committed/closing but not yet funded, and the company runs underwater the whole way.
prediction.likely_lead: Ben Franklin Technology Partners (C&N PA) anchoring (~$100K econ-dev check), with Schematic Ventures ($150K) and 640 Oxford ($150K) filling the partial round; Robin Hood Ventures warm via BFTP
prediction.terms_estimate: Priced preferred, ~$3.5–4M pre-money (repriced down from the $5M / $500K ask); min-viable close $300K, realistic partial $300–400K of the $500K target
prediction.timeline: Indicative interest crosses min-viable (~$300K) around month 4–5; round 'triggers to close' month 6; proceeds land month 7 after the 1-month close lag and trigger the first hire (customer-facing engineer) in month 8.

founder_millionaire.note: PAPER stays null in-horizon: although the round triggers/closes at month 6, the ledger shows raise_injected:false and founder_paper_net_worth_usd:$0 for all six months — the priced mark is only realized once proceeds actually land (month 7, out of horizon). Even then, a fundraise marks PAPER (~$3.5–4M × ~99% post-dilution ownership) but yields ~$0 LIQUID. LIQUID stays null throughout: founder draws $0 salary (ARR $8.8K << $255K trigger), there is no exit and no secondary, so the slow organic (salary − lifestyle) path contributes nothing yet.

financial_outlook.one_liner: Six months of pure burn on $0 opening cash — recurring MRR climbs to a thin $730/mo while episodic $8K Ratatosk diagnostics keep two months cash-positive, but the company is underwater every month (ending cash −$6.6K) and the closing pre-seed funds in month 7, just past the horizon.

report.causal_narrative: With $0 opening cash, Mimir is underwater from month 1; the only thing keeping it alive is event-driven services cash — two $8K Ratatosk diagnostics (months 2 and 4) flip those months net-positive, but the off months bleed the steady ~$3,735 non-draw OpEx against negligible MRR, leaving ending cash at −$6,641. Fixing the critical data-loss blocker (YGGDATA-258) and broken business-flow transitions unlocked the first paid diagnostic, a design-partner LOI, and a first Norn seat, which in turn moved BFTP, Schematic, Robin Hood, and 640 Oxford toward a closing partial round at month 6. The crucial reconciliation: the ledger never injects the raise (raise_injected:false all six months, paper net worth $0) because the priced close carries a 1-month lag — it triggers in month 6 but funds in month 7, so in-horizon the runway stays negative and the company survives on services float, not on the round. SOC 2 still not being ready and the food/beverage Yggdrasil pilot being SOC-2-contingent are the brakes that keep recurring revenue thin and several investors (DataTribe, Differential, Stage 2) on the sidelines.
caveats: The month log narrative says the round 'closes' at month 6, but the authoritative ledger shows raise_injected:false and founder_paper_net_worth_usd:$0 for ALL six months — so no cash injection or paper mark is realized in-horizon. The close/funding lands in month 7 due to the 1-month close lag. Treat the in-horizon raise as committed-but-not-funded.

Ending cash is negative (−$6,641) every month after month 1; the company is technically insolvent on a cash basis throughout and only survives by timing $8K diagnostics against monthly OpEx. A single missed diagnostic or a 1-month slip in the raise creates a real cash-out event that the model papers over.
Runway_months in the ledger is mechanically negative (or 999 in cash-positive months) because cash is negative — it is not a meaningful 'months of runway' figure; read it as 'already underwater.'

MRR is extremely thin ($730/mo = $8.8K ARR) — three orders of magnitude below the $255K founder-draw trigger and the $500K seed milestone. The 6-month revenue is overwhelmingly one-time services ($16K diagnostics) plus a contingent $35K Yggdrasil pilot booking, not durable recurring revenue.

The Yggdrasil pilot ($35K, signed month 5) is contingent on SOC 2 Type 1 readiness, which is still in Phase 3 with three controls not started — if SOC 2 slips, that pilot revenue and the food/beverage prospect both fall away.

The raise probability (0.55) and partial-vs-full split are sensitive: gates for several investors (paid LOIs, production deploy, SOC 2) remain unmet, so the realistic outcome is a partial $300–400K, not the full $500K ask.

Founder is solo (1 FTE, the binding constraint); the first hire only triggers post-funding (month 8), so execution capacity stays maxed out through the entire horizon, capping how fast blockers clear and pilots deploy.
coalitions: Capital / closing syndicate (month 6): Ben Franklin Technology Partners C&N PA (~$100K anchor, engaged) + Schematic Ventures ($150K, interested) + 640 Oxford ($150K, interested) + Robin Hood Ventures (warm via BFTP, interested) — the partial-round coalition.

Capital / on-the-fence, traction-gated: Ben Franklin statewide (curious), Ironspring (curious, needs production deploy), Work-Bench (curious, needs enterprise logos), Stage 2 Capital (curious, needs paid LOIs).
Capital / thesis-blocked by SOC 2 + data-loss: Differential Ventures (skeptical, data-infra unproven), DataTribe (cold, security/compliance unproven).

Revenue-generating customer coalition: South-Central PA precision metal fabricator (engaged, two $8K Ratatosk diagnostics) + CNC/contract machine shop (design-partner LOI signed) + industrial distributor (Norn paid seat, $140/mo MRR).
SOC-2-contingent / not-yet-converted: South-Central PA food/beverage processor (curious; $35K Yggdrasil pilot signed but gated on SOC 2 Type 1 readiness).

swing_factors.factor: 1-month raise close lag vs. the 6-month horizon
swing_factors.why: The round triggers in month 6 but funds in month 7. The entire 'raise closes in-horizon' answer hinges on whether you count the trigger or the wire — the ledger counts the wire (raise_injected:false), so cash never resets before the horizon ends.
With $0 opening cash and ~$3,735/mo OpEx, the two diagnostics in months 2 and 4 are the only thing preventing a hard cash-out. Slipping either by a month turns survival into insolvency.

Gates the $35K Yggdrasil pilot conversion, the $2.5K/mo subscription that would meaningfully lift MRR, and the conviction of security-thesis investors (DataTribe, Differential). It is still Phase 3 with three controls not started.

swing_factors.factor: Open critical/high blockers (YGGDATA-258 data loss, 262 broken transitions, 144 email)
swing_factors.why: Clearing 258 and 262 unlocked the first paid diagnostic and the design-partner LOI; remaining gaps and thin test coverage keep prospects 'evaluating' and cap willingness to sign or deploy in production.

swing_factors.factor: Size of the partial close ($300K min-viable vs. $500K ask)
swing_factors.why: Determines post-raise runway and whether the first hire and SOC 2 audit outlay are affordable. A bare $300K close leaves little margin after the $20K SOC 2 audit and $110K/yr hire.

First hire is post-funding (month 8). Through the whole horizon the founder must simultaneously fix blockers, run SOC 2, deliver diagnostics, and fundraise — any one slipping cascades into the others.

paper.basis: ownership × marked valuation (priced round pre-money $4000000, or acquisition price). ILLIQUID; SAFE/notes do not mark until conversion.

liquid.basis: actual founder cash: acquisition cash-out + founder secondary + slow (salary − lifestyle) accrual. Founder draws $0 until ARR ≥ 3× the $85K base ($255K), so the salary path contributes nothing early. A priced fundraise yields $0 liquid — proceeds go to the company. Reaching $1M via salary alone is a multi-year climb.
